notes: J0546: only the abbreviated label J0546 is supplied (I:p3-b0); no full coordinate designation or individual velocity is given. J1332: same, only the abbreviated label in I:p3-b0. J1603: only the abbreviated label in I:p6-b4. J1109: only the abbreviated label in I:p6-b4. J1311: only the abbreviated label in I:p6-b4. J1637+3631: described only as a likely additional D6 star and omitted from Fig. 1 because its luminosity is not accurately known (T:p3-b6). J0905+2510: omitted from Fig. 3 because its distance and luminosity are poorly constrained (T:p6-b6); included as part of the LP 40-365 sample. J1825-3757: explicitly still bound to the Milky Way (T:p8-b2), but retained as follow_up because the paper studies it among the LP 40-365 stars from prior work (T:p6-b6). J1240+6710: only a possible LP 40-365 member and explicitly still bound (T:p6-b6, T:p8-b2); retained as follow_up, not as a current unbound candidate. LP 40-365: the class is called hypervelocity survivors (T:p2-b6), but individual present-day bound/unbound status is not stated for the class members other than the explicit bound exceptions J1825-3757 and J1240+6710. D6-1, D6-2, D6-3, J0927-6335, J1235-3752: all are previously known D6 candidates and are therefore classified as follow_up rather than newly found candidates.

D6-1: The paper discusses D6-1's luminosity, effective temperature, age, and possible model mass (e.g., T:p3-b8, T:p4-b4, I:p3-b0), but it does not report right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for D6-1. The 2300 km/s value in T:p7-b2 is an assumed ejection velocity for a model population described as appropriate for D6-1, D6-3, and possibly J1235-3752, not an individual measured present-day Galactic-rest-frame velocity for D6-1; under the rules it is not assigned as an individual result.

D6-2: D6-2: The paper reports an ejection velocity of 1050 km/s (T:p5-b9; also T:p7-b2 and I:p7-b6), but does not identify it as a line-of-sight radial velocity or as the total three-dimensional speed in the Galactic rest frame. No eligible position, parallax, distance, proper-motion, galactocentric-radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for D6-2, so no quantities are extracted.

D6-3: D6-3 is discussed in the text and shown in Figures 1 and 5, but the paper does not report values for any requested quantity (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) for D6-3. The 2300 km s^-1 value at T:p7-b2 is an adopted model ejection velocity for a population including D6-1 and D6-3, not a reported Galactic rest-frame velocity for D6-3.

J0927-6335: J0927-6335 is discussed only qualitatively or graphically: its effective temperature and luminosity appear as an error bar in Figure 1, and its midplane travel time is described as negative. The paper does not report an eligible quantity (RA, Dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability) specifically for J0927-6335. The general survivor velocities mentioned in the text (e.g., >1000 km/s, 2300 km/s, 1050 km/s) are population/model values and are not assigned to J0927-6335. See T:p3-b0, T:p3-b4, T:p3-b6, and T:p1-b7.

J1235-3752: J1235-3752 is discussed qualitatively in T:p3-b4, T:p3-b8, T:p4-b5, T:p5-b3, and T:p7-b2, and its position/age range appear in I:p3-b0 and I:p7-b7. The paper does not report numerical values for any of the requested quantities for this star. Figure 1 shows its luminosity and effective temperature, which are not requested quantities. The 2300 km s^-1 value in T:p7-b2 is a model ejection velocity adopted for a population that may include J1235-3752, not a reported line-of-sight radial velocity or total Galactic-rest-frame speed for the star.

J1637+3631: J1637+3631 is mentioned only in T:p3-b6: "J1637+3631, discovered by Raddi et al. (2019) and likely another D6 star (Hollands et al., in preparation), is not shown as it does not have an accurate luminosity estimate." The paper reports no position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for this star. Therefore no quantities are extracted.

J0546: J0546 appears in the supplied material only as a labeled error bar in the luminosity–effective-temperature diagrams (I:p3-b0 and I:p4-b6). The paper does not report numerical right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for J0546. The text mentions that effective temperatures and luminosities for the three hottest D6 stars come from Werner et al. (2024), with luminosities rescaled using SED and Gaia distances, but gives no numerical astrometric or velocity values for this star.

J1332: J1332 appears only as a labeled error bar in Figures 1 and 2 (I:p3-b0, I:p4-b6); the paper gives no numerical right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for this star. The plotted quantities are luminosity and effective temperature only, which are not among the requested quantities.

LP 40-365: The paper identifies LP 40-365 (GD 492) as the namesake of the LP 40-365 class of hypervelocity stars (T:p2-b6). Figure 3 (I:p6-b4) plots the class members' luminosities and effective temperatures, but the paper does not report right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probabilities for LP 40-365 itself. No requested quantity can therefore be extracted.

J1603: J1603 appears only in Figure 3 (I:p6-b4), where its luminosity and effective temperature are plotted as an error bar among the LP 40-365 stars; the text states these properties are taken from Raddi et al. (2019) and El-Badry et al. (2023) (T:p6-b6). The paper does not report any of the requested quantities (coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability) for J1603 in the supplied material.

J1109: J1109 appears only in Figure 3 (I:p6-b4) as an error bar in the luminosity–effective temperature plane, among the LP 40-365 stars whose properties are taken from Raddi et al. (2019) and El-Badry et al. (2023). The paper does not report any of the requested quantities (coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability) for J1109, and luminosity/effective temperature are not among the requested quantity identifiers.

J1311: J1311 appears only in Figure 3 (I:p6-b4), where its luminosity and effective temperature are shown as an error bar among the LP 40-365 stars. The paper does not report any of the eligible quantities (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability) for J1311.

J1825-3757: J1825-3757 appears in T:p6-b7, I:p6-b4, and T:p8-b2. The paper discusses its position in a luminosity–effective-temperature diagram and states qualitatively that it is still bound to the Milky Way, but it reports no eligible numerical values for right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability.

J1240+6710: J1240+6710 is discussed only qualitatively: it is a possible LP 40-365 member whose age is unknown and which is still bound to the Galaxy; no numeric values for the requested quantities are reported (T:p6-b6, T:p8-b2). I:p6-b4 shows it in a luminosity–effective-temperature diagram, but that does not provide any of the target quantities.

J0905+2510: The target star J0905+2510 is mentioned only at T:p6-b6, where the authors state: "We do not display J0905+2510, as its distance and thus luminosity are not well-constrained." No numerical values for any requested quantity (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) are reported or adopted for this star in the supplied material. Figure 3 (I:p6-b4) likewise does not include J0905+2510. Therefore no quantities are submitted.
